frame_metadata.gps_note: First take with GPS on every frame. App frames carry a 9-key GPS block written by the F0 build; stock-camera HEICs carry Apple's full 15-key block. Both bind the frame to the Met to within a few metres.

source_note: App frames are camera-roll copies (Image Capture over USB) bound to the manifest by capture time with tools/manifest/bind-frames.py — see derived/2026-09-20-met-frames.json. The app's label frame (HWFN5677) is out of focus; the transcription is from the stock-camera retake shot 30 s later. Keep both: the pair is the focus-failure regression case for F1.

expected.title: Marble funerary lekythos of Aristomache
expected.date_edtf_note: BCE years are astronomical: 375 BCE is -0374. Ranges are intervals; '~' marks each end when the label says 'ca.'. A named span like 'late 6th century' is written as the conventional interval and noted in date_raw.
expected.medium_note: Only in the title on the label; the API says 'Marble, Pentelic'.
expected.findspot: Said to have been found near the Kerameikos in Athens
expected.inscription: Inscribed above the large standing figures, from left to right, Stratokleia Aiolos Aristomache Axiomache; below the seated woman, Leonike
expected.condition: Restored foot, mouth, and most of neck and handle

traps.date_looks_like_an_accession: On-device OCR of the soft frame offered '373-350' and '375-350' — the date range — as the accession, and the human corrected it to 49.11.4. Two three-digit numbers joined by a dash is a BCE date on every Greek and Roman label in this gallery; score that shape down. The donation year 1949 agreeing with '49.' is the positive signal.
traps.focus: The app frame reads 'Purchase, Joseph Pulitzer Bequest, 1949 (49.11.4)' at 12 lines with 11 contested; the stock frame reads all of it clean. Same label, same phone, 30 seconds apart. See docs/field-beta.md findings.
